reason: Both alerts are TP. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input from request.getParameterValues() flows through param -> bar (always assigned param due to conditional (500/42)+196=207>200) -> sql -> encodeForHTML(sql) -> response.getWriter().println(), with resolved sink value being attacker-controlled (encoded user input). Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): User input flows through param -> bar -> sql -> batchUpdate(sql), with resolved sink value being attacker-controlled (unescaped user input concatenated into SQL query string). Both represent real vulnerabilities.

evidence.note: XSS sink: response.getWriter().println() outputs encodeForHTML(sql) containing user input from param
SQL injection sink: batchUpdate(sql) executes query with user input concatenated into password field
